_about: Optional written view per upcoming game, keyed by ESPN game id: {"text": "...", "sources": [urls], "written_at": ISO}. Shown on the game page as 'Analyst view' (locker-room news, trade rumours, a player facing his former team...). Never mixed into the numbers.

401910023.text: Milwaukee's 12-game losing streak is the club's longest since 1996. The last two losses were emotional 'reunion' games against Giannis Antetokounmpo and Damian Lillard. Taylor Jenkins has admitted that what the team is doing 'is not working', and Myles Turner and Kyle Kuzma are both out with shoulder injuries. Philadelphia are rolling, and LeBron James called the Orlando win one of their best of the season, though Tyrese Maxey and Jaylen Brown were questionable. The angle leans clearly towards Philadelphia.

401910024.text: The defending champion Knicks open a five-game homestand, while Portland are on game five of a six-game road trip right after Damian Lillard's emotional 33-point return to Milwaukee. The Blazers are still without Ja Morant (hamstring) and Shaedon Sharpe, Deni Avdija is questionable, and they have lost seven straight to New York. The angle leans towards New York.

401910025.text: The Clippers are 0-6 on the road and just lost to a three-win Utah team. Brandon Ingram is still out, with his debut reportedly targeted for Monday against Houston, and Bradley Beal has no timeline. Derrick Jones Jr. faces his former team. Dallas snapped a three-game skid by beating Golden State, have Kyrie Irving back, and Dusty May wants that physicality 'every night'. The angle leans towards Dallas.

401910026.text: Memphis have won five straight and are 8-0 on the road. Ty Jerome was upgraded to probable after a hip issue, though Cameron Boozer, Jerami Grant and others are out. Minnesota are still without Anthony Edwards after knee surgery and come off a late collapse at the Knicks, when they went scoreless after cutting a 16-point deficit to three. The angle leans slightly towards Memphis.

401910027.text: New Orleans are in turmoil: the club confirmed Dejounte Murray's trade request, and Jamahl Mosley's lineup choices are under fire. The night before, they blew a 16-point lead at OKC to fall to 0-3 in the Cup, so this is the second night of a back-to-back with travel. San Antonio are rested, though Dylan Harper is out for a few weeks. The angle leans towards San Antonio.

401910028.text: Boston are on their first two-game skid of the season after blowing a 17-point lead at Denver, and players called the problems 'correctable'. Jayson Tatum is questionable for rest and Derrick White with a new shoulder issue, with Golden State on Sunday. Sacramento are 0-9 at home and on a back-to-back after a narrow loss to the Lakers, and Doug Christie says his seat is 'hot always'. The angle leans towards Boston, but less so if the Celtics rest their stars.

401910029.text: Detroit lost to Toronto on the second night of a back-to-back and are missing Jalen Duren, Duncan Robinson and Ron Holland, though Cade Cunningham is back from knee soreness. J.B. Bickerstaff says he won't rush the injured players. Atlanta have won three straight but lost CJ McCollum for at least four weeks, and rookie Kingston Flemings has back tightness. The angle leans slightly towards Atlanta at home.

401910030.text: Miami have won six straight, and a team source says 'we want to win now'. Rival executives expect the Heat to add a guard. OKC are badly depleted, with Jalen Williams, Chet Holmgren and Cason Wallace out long-term and Alex Caruso hurt. This is their second road game in three nights after a comeback in New Orleans. The angle leans towards Miami.

401910031.text: Orlando come in on a high after Franz Wagner's game-winner against his brother's Nets, and they have a revenge motive after losing to Washington on Nov 2. Paolo Banchero is still out with what he calls a 'complex' ankle injury. Anthony Davis had 36 and 11 in Washington's win in Chicago, and he is playing for a contract after reports that a max extension is unlikely. The angle is close to neutral.

401910032.text: Denver have won six of eight, including a 17-point comeback against Boston and a strong finish against Houston, and former Bull DeMar DeRozan returns to Chicago. The Bulls blew a 15-point lead to lose at home to Washington. Caleb Wilson is out until around Christmas, and Josh Giddey's hold on the starting job is being questioned after a fourth-quarter benching. The angle leans towards Denver.

401910033.text: Dallas are framed as 'ahead of schedule' under first-year coach Dusty May, with Kyrie Irving back, but they play the second night of a back-to-back. Utah lost to Phoenix after briefly breaking a 12-game skid, with Lauri Markkanen and Jaren Jackson Jr. out without timelines. Rookie Darryn Peterson is being managed carefully. The owner says Will Hardy's job is safe. The angle leans slightly towards Dallas.

401910034.text: Indiana keep losing guards: T.J. McConnell left Friday's loss with a hamstring issue, Tyrese Haliburton has no timetable, and the Pacers host OKC the next night. The Knicks are on a back-to-back. Mitchell Robinson is unhappy after a move to the bench, and Karl-Anthony Towns is reportedly using the stalled extension talks as motivation. The angle leans towards New York.

401910035.text: Golden State came home from an 0-5 road trip. Steve Kerr says the team is 'wiped out with injuries': Stephen Curry (oblique), Jimmy Butler and Kristaps Porzingis are out, and Draymond Green has an elbow issue. Boston play the second night of a back-to-back after Sacramento, and Jayson Tatum and Derrick White were already questionable, so rest days are a real risk. The angle leans towards Boston on morale, depending on who plays.
